questions.question: Explain the difference between linear and non-linear dramatic structure, giving an example of each.

points.text: Linear: events in time order (e.g. An Inspector Calls has a linear investigation). Non-linear: out of time order (e.g. Blood Brothers uses flashforward opening). Must explain the different effects each creates.

questions.question: How does a cyclical structure affect the audience's understanding of a play's themes?

points.text: Cyclical structure suggests events are inescapable — the audience knows the outcome from the start, creating dramatic irony and a sense of fate. E.g. Blood Brothers opens and closes with the twins' death.

questions.question: Compare tragedy and comedy as dramatic genres. How do they use different techniques to engage the audience?

points.text: Tragedy uses hamartia, catharsis and peripeteia to evoke pity and fear; comedy uses misunderstanding, wit and physical humour to entertain. Both engage through different emotional routes.
